description: We’re Earth-616, a team of five joining NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We love building creative, useful, and visually engaging projects with real-world data. For the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, we’re exploring how NASA’s Earth data can become an interactive experience through visualization, sound, web technologies, and AI. 🌍
summary:
EARTH-616 is an interactive Earth exploration experience developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Earth Information Jukebox. It transforms complex environmental information into an engaging experience by connecting an interactive 3D Earth, historical scientific visualizations, synchronized data charts, and sonification.

Users can explore historical global temperature anomalies, atmospheric CO₂ concentrations, and global mean sea-level observations through a shared timeline. NASA's temperature visualization provides a geographic perspective, while charts help users examine long-term environmental changes. Through the Web Audio API, selected scientific values are translated into synthesized sounds, offering another way to perceive patterns in Earth's changing systems.

EARTH-616 addresses the challenge by combining visual and auditory representations of Earth information in one accessible experience. Rather than presenting environmental data as isolated numbers, it encourages people to explore, compare, and experience scientific information.

We believe understanding our planet should not be limited to researchers or scientific reports. By making Earth data more interactive and approachable, EARTH-616 aims to inspire curiosity, improve public engagement with Earth science, and encourage a deeper connection with our changing planet.
details:
Project Details - EARTH-616

EARTH-616 is an interactive web-based Earth exploration platform that brings together scientific data, 3D visualization, synchronized timelines, and data sonification to help people experience and understand changes in our planet.

What It Does and How It Works

The application presents an interactive 3D Earth with atmospheric effects, clouds, and contextual surface textures. Users can explore historical environmental information through a shared timeline that connects available visualizations and data charts.

EARTH-616 integrates three major environmental indicators:

  • Global Temperature: Monthly global temperature anomalies from NASA GISTEMP v4, covering 1880–2026 in the local dataset.
  • Atmospheric CO₂: Monthly measurements from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory, covering 1958–2026 in the local dataset.
  • Global Mean Sea Level: Weekly observations from NASA-SSH / PO.DAAC, covering 1993–2026 in the local dataset.

For geographic temperature visualization, the platform uses NASA Scientific Visualization Studio's historical temperature anomaly frames. Synchronized charts allow users to explore changes across the available timeline.

A central feature is data sonification. Using the Web Audio API, selected environmental measurements are translated into synthesized audio frequencies. Users can listen to individual indicators or explore a combined temperature and CO₂ representation. This provides an additional way to perceive patterns that might otherwise remain abstract in numerical datasets.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EARTH-616 aims to make Earth science more accessible to students, educators, and the general public. By combining visual exploration with sound, it offers multiple ways to engage with environmental information.

Its intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, support informal learning, and help people develop a stronger understanding of long-term environmental changes.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the platform using JavaScript, Next.js, and React. Three.js and React Three Fiber power the interactive 3D Earth, while Tailwind CSS and Framer Motion support the interface and animations. Recharts handles data visualization, and the Web Audio API generates the sonification.

We also used publicly available NASA and NOAA datasets and NASA SVS visualization assets. Development was supported by AI tools including GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and ChatGPT.

Creativity and Team Considerations

Our creative approach is to treat environmental information as something people can explore and experience rather than simply read. Connecting a 3D globe, historical data, synchronized charts, and synthesized sound creates a unified learning experience.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, missing observations, temporal alignment, accessibility, performance, and usability. We distinguished global-average measurements from geographically resolved visualizations and documented limitations where exact historical alignment or complete independent data verification was unavailable.

EARTH-616 demonstrates how scientific information can become more engaging through the combination of interactive technology, visual storytelling, and sound.
